text.text_excerpt: During a walk ab out last night I stopped in the new location with a friend to check things out. I walked in and immediately exclaimed "I love that smell!" And as you give me that same look my friend gave me, no, it is not the pungent smell of weed wafting in on the night breezes but the heady scent of natural herbs and oils used for healing that so permeated my youth in the mountains. It smells like every herbal health food I've ever walked into since I was a kid. I love that smell! I also love the new venue and am a bit sad actually that they will be moving to the old location up the street (as soon as this Monday the clerk told me), but I'm sure there are many reasons for that.... like...

This is about as alternative as you can find in the greater New Orleans area. The parking is all street parking in this area, but as most of the neighbors are cemeteries, its not too difficult to find a spot. It is right next to a coffee shop which is cool. They have a variety of incense, essential oils, lotions, hemp and CBD items. I was looking for something for my younger sister who is a bit on the earthy side, and I was able to find some incense for her to use while she was in town, which was perfection. They do have bundles of sage if you are into smudging your house of the evil spirits lurking around the corner. This shop has quite a bit of inventory and I think the customer service...

This is one of the only shops in the city that sells Wild Harvest herbs, a brand I rely on, so I was exceedingly pleased to discover them there yesterday. They have a lot of other goodies as well, to suit a variety of needs. Teas, prayer candles, incense, kratom, goofer dust, whatever the heart desires. The folks who run it seem friendly and it has a comforting clean smell. And the attached cafe... boy oh boy. Best caramel frappe I've had in ages.
